Jordan / team — I started assembling the artifacts and attached initial drafts. Quick answers first:

- Subprocessors in scope for EU customer data:
  * AWS (S3, RDS) - primary long-term storage (transfers within EU regions; cross-border when backups replicated to us-central for DR)
  * GCP (AI training pipelines for certain opt-ins) - not used by default for Nimbus but flagged if customer enables training
  * Datadog - telemetry only (no PII persisted)
  * HashiCorp Vault (managed) - key material storage (KMS abstraction layer)
  * Sentry - error reports (PII redaction applied)

- Key custody: primary KMS for production is AWS KMS (customer data keys are envelope-encrypted; mixed custody model: Redwood-managed CMKs for hosted customers; for Dedicated/Private customers we offer customer-managed keys via KMS integrations). KMS attestation attached.

- Retention: see attached redwood-retention-matrix.xlsx (draft). High-level: ephemeral inference caches (<=48 hrs), short-term telemetry logs (30 days), long-term audit logs (365 days) unless customer-specific retention overrides.

I attached: annotated-dataflow-v1.pdf (draft) and retention workbook. Please review and add technical callouts for cache/KV layers and streaming inference paths.

Mina Haddad
Director, Privacy & Trust — Redwood Inference

Adding a few technical clarifications to Mina’s draft:

- Cache/KV details: Inference KV cache is per-request, stored in GPU-hosted ephemeral cache (not persisted). We have an optional prefix cache backed by Redis for high-throughput customers — Redis is hosted in EU regions for EU customers by default. If Redis is used for Nimbus we will ensure it is pinned to eu-west-1 and use VPC peering.

- Cross-border replication: Backups for S3/RDS are replicated to us-east-1 for DR; we can disable cross-region replication for Nimbus if required (trade-off with recovery point objective).

- Encryption at rest/in transit: All internal services enforce TLS 1.2+; data at rest encrypted with AES-256; envelope encryption uses AWS KMS CMKs. The kms-attestation-2026-11.txt confirms CMK lifecycle audits.

- Suggested edits to the flow PDF: call out the model-serving fallback to quantized CPU instances (no persistent PII there), mark telemetry sinks as "redacted" in the diagram. I made inline callouts in the Drive link.

I updated the retention matrix with technical retention flags and added a tab listing subprocessors + contracts.

Let me know if we should produce a short cover email summarizing the trade-offs (recommended: disable cross-region replication for Nimbus and provide cust-managed CMK if they require strict key custody).

Karthik Iyer
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
